# Wasif Faisal - Payment Security Researcher

> Wasif Faisal (also known as Md. Wasif Faisal; online handle @cswasif) is an independent cybersecurity researcher specializing in payment security, cyber threat intelligence, transaction protocol analysis, and EMV 3-D Secure (3DS) vulnerabilities.

## Core Specializations
- **Payment Authentication Protocols**: Empirical vulnerability discovery in browser-mediated EMV 3-D Secure 2.x flows, identifying pre-authorization authentication oracles and client-visible classification channels.
- **Adversarial Ecosystems & Threat Intelligence**: In-the-wild tracking of automated BIN attacks, card-testing infrastructure, rotating residential proxy evasion, and underground payment fraud tools since 2018.
- **Transaction Protocol Analysis & Reissuance**: Statistical modeling of card reissuance prefix collisions, fraud boundaries, and financial authorization rail separation.

## Key Research Monographs & Publications
- **The 3DS Oracle: BIN Attack via the Network** (arXiv:2610.32206 [cs.CR], Oct 2026)
  - Authors: Wasif Faisal, Suprava Saha Dibya.
  - Abstract & Links: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32206 | PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32206
  - Technical Summary: Demonstrates that browser-mediated 3-D Secure 2.x flows expose pre-authorization authentication continuation oracles, allowing off-context attackers to harvest or screen card numbers at scale before financial authorization.
- **Prefix Count Limits Can Increase First-Hit Discovery in Card Reissuance** (arXiv:2609.31398 [cs.CR], Sep 2026)
  - Author: Wasif Faisal.
  - Abstract & Links: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31398 | PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.31398
  - Technical Summary: Simulates 50,000 synthetic candidates to prove that issuer prefix caps can counterintuitively increase first-hit discovery probability during automated BIN testing.

## Academic Background & Service
- **Education**: B.Sc. in Computer Science, BRAC University (Summer 2026). Thesis: *CNP-SHIELD: Card-Not-Present Vulnerabilities in Payment Gateways*, supervised by Md. Akhtaruzzaman Adnan and Prof. S. M. Taiabul Haque, PhD.
- **Professional Service**: Artifact Evaluation Program Committee Reviewer, ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS 2026-B).
